knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Work outside training or authorisation is stopped and escalated to the supervisor before going further. Continuing in the current clothing or substituting a branded shirt or other item is not an acceptable way to proceed.

Noting the defect, replacing the unsafe item and telling the supervisor is the correct handover. The check-record-escalate step requires a factual handover to the named contact with the item recorded, so the defect is not hidden. Wearing the defective item, hiding it or waiting without telling anyone are not acceptable.

Picking task-specific PPE from the risk assessment, product label and site procedure is the correct decision. PPE is chosen for the task rather than from habit, what is nearest, or a branded shirt. Reusing the same gloves for every product ignores each product's hazard.
A branded shirt is not protection against splashes. Relying on it instead of PPE chosen from the risk assessment, product label and site procedure is the unsafe alternative.
Unsafe clothing is replaced, and the lesson requires replacement before the next hazardous task. Replacement is documented when required.

practicalCriteria: Checks the site/task requirements before acting
Identifies and applies relevant safety and privacy controls
Communicates professionally and respects authorisation boundaries
Records the outcome and escalates unresolved issues correctly
passRule: All safety-critical criteria must be demonstrated; remediate and reassess any missed criterion.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 4: Keep normal uniform separate from protective equipment, and do not treat a branded shirt as splash protection.
Record of procedure step 6: Replace clothing that is torn, contaminated or unsafe, and note the defect.
Record of procedure step 7: Keep a spare clean layer where a shift involves changing environments or customer-facing work.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 4 is not done: Keep normal uniform separate from protective equipment, and do not treat a branded shirt as splash protection.
Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: Replace clothing that is torn, contaminated or unsafe, and note the defect.
Stop work if procedure step 8 is not done: Stop and ask the supervisor before going further if a task falls outside your training or authority.
